scenarios.title: Business Social Media Account Takeover
scenarios.attacker_objective: Gain control of a business social media account and use that control to impersonate the business and potentially deceive customers.

questions.story:
2:16 PM — An Unexpected Security Alert

You manage your business's social media account. While preparing a normal business post, your phone displays: “New login detected.” You did not log in from a new device.

A few minutes later, you notice that some account-security or recovery information has changed even though you did not change it.
questions.question: What is your first assessment of the situation?
options: It is probably a normal platform update.
It may indicate unauthorized access to the business account.
The platform is automatically improving your business profile.
It means one of your customers has placed an order.
questions.feedback: An unfamiliar login together with unexpected account-security changes is a strong indication that someone else may have accessed the account.

questions.story:
2:23 PM — The Account Starts Acting Strangely

You notice that a new message has been sent from the business account to several customers. One customer replies: “Why are you asking me to click this link?” You did not send the message.

You check the account again and find that the profile or recovery details are no longer exactly as you left them.
questions.question: What does the new information tell you?
options: The platform has automatically sent a marketing campaign.
The account may have been taken over and is now being used to impersonate the business.
The customers have accidentally changed the account.
The business has received too many messages.
questions.feedback: Messages being sent without the owner's action, combined with unexpected account changes, strongly suggests that an unauthorized person may control the account.

questions.story:
2:29 PM — The Attacker Reveals the Objective

You receive a WhatsApp message from someone claiming to be helping you recover the account.

They say: “Your account has been compromised. I can secure it for you. Send me the login code you just received so I can cancel the attack.”

At the same time, you can still see unfamiliar activity on the business account.
questions.question: What is happening?
options: The support agent is helping you recover the account.
The platform is performing a routine security check.
The attacker is using impersonation to obtain an authentication code and maintain or gain control of the business account.
The customer messages are causing the account to malfunction.
questions.feedback: The request for an authentication code from an unverified person is consistent with an account-takeover attempt. The code should not be disclosed.
